seoTitle: How to Fix a Temporarily Locked PayPal Account (2026)
metaDescription: PayPal explains exactly why an account gets limited and what lifts it, once you know which screen to check. Here's the Resolution Center walkthrough, sourced from PayPal's own help articles.
intro: A locked or limited PayPal account freezes your ability to send or receive money right when you need it most, and a red restriction banner tends to make people click around at random instead of following the actual fix. PayPal's own help documentation is specific about what triggers a limitation and what removes it. The trick is knowing which screen carries that information. This guide walks through finding the reason for the lock, verifying your identity through the right account screens, and what to do if you can't even reach the login page.
prerequisites: Access to the email inbox or phone number tied to your PayPal account, since that's how PayPal confirms you own it.
A government-issued ID and, if asked, a proof of address dated within the last 12 months, in case identity verification turns out to be part of the fix.

steps.heading: Check your notifications before you touch anything else
steps.body: Log in at paypal.com and click the bell icon in the top navigation before trying to send money or edit anything. PayPal's own explanation of limitations groups the usual causes into four buckets: regulatory requirements triggered by something like a debit card request, a violation of the Acceptable Use Policy, fraud protection after an unauthorized login or a bank alert, and high-risk seller activity such as a spike in chargebacks or a sudden jump in sales volume. The notification tells you which of these applies to your account, and it usually links straight into the relevant checklist.

steps.heading: Open your account settings to see what's on file
steps.body: Click the gear icon next to Log Out to reach account settings, which opens on the Account tab showing your profile, join date, linked emails, phone numbers, and addresses. Worth a scan even before dealing with the lock: a stale email, phone number, or address is a common reason automated compliance checks flag an account. Update anything that looks wrong before submitting verification documents, so the two don't contradict each other.

image.caption: The Account tab inside PayPal's settings, showing linked emails, phone numbers, and addresses alongside tabs for Security, Payments, and Seller Tools.

steps.heading: Move to the Security tab to reset credentials
steps.body: From the same settings area, click over to Security. This is where you reset a password and review login activity, useful if the lock followed several failed sign-in attempts, since resetting the password here is faster than waiting out any automatic timeout. Check for unrecognized devices or sessions while you're in this tab; an unfamiliar login is often what triggered the restriction in the first place.

image.caption: The Security tab in account settings, the place to reset a password or review recent login activity.

steps.heading: Go to Help, then Resolution Center
steps.body: Click Help in the main navigation and select Resolution Center. This lists every open item PayPal needs from you as a separate row: identity verification and a funding-source confirmation, for example, often show up as two distinct tasks instead of one combined request. Click Resolve next to an active row to open its specific form instead of guessing what's needed.

steps.heading: Confirm your identity
steps.body: PayPal offers two ways to do this. On the PayPal app, it can scan your government-issued ID and your face with your phone's camera and compare the two. On a computer, you upload a photo of your ID plus a proof of address dated within the last 12 months, both showing your name clearly and, for the ID, all four corners of the document. A blurry or partial scan is the most common reason verification gets kicked back for resubmission, which adds days to the process.

steps.heading: Submit and track the review
steps.body: Once documents are attached, submit them. PayPal says it tries to review submissions within two business days, though some cases take longer, and it emails you at each stage. Check the inbox tied to your account's primary address, not a secondary one. If all the listed steps are already done and the account is still limited, it means PayPal has already reviewed it and is waiting on more information by email, or the review is still in progress.

steps.heading: If you can't even reach the login screen
steps.body: Go to Contact Us on paypal.com, select Call Us near the bottom, then choose "Call us as a guest" to see the phone number. Have three things ready to confirm ownership: the phone number on the account, a statement for the linked bank account or card, and the email address you registered with. This route exists specifically for people who've already tried resetting their password and still can't sign in.

troubleshooting.problem: The Resolution Center shows nothing, but an email says the account is limited
troubleshooting.cause: The email is very likely fraudulent. A genuine limitation always shows up as a row in the Resolution Center.
troubleshooting.fix: Forward the email to phishing@paypal.com, then delete it. If you clicked a link or opened an attachment, log in directly, review recent payments, and change your password.

troubleshooting.problem: Uploaded identity documents keep getting rejected
troubleshooting.cause: Usually a blurry photo, a cropped ID with corners missing, or a proof of address older than 12 months.
troubleshooting.fix: Try the PayPal app's biometric scan instead of a manual upload, or re-photograph the documents in good light with the full page visible.

troubleshooting.problem: Every Resolution Center step is marked complete, and the account is still limited
troubleshooting.cause: PayPal has already reviewed the submission and sent a follow-up request by email, or the review is simply still running.
troubleshooting.fix: Check email, including spam, for a specific follow-up request. If nothing arrives and enough time has passed, contact support directly instead of resubmitting the same documents.

troubleshooting.problem: A password reset doesn't fix the lockout
troubleshooting.cause: The restriction is tied to something other than failed logins, a fraud flag or a compliance hold, for instance, so it doesn't clear on its own.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the Resolution Center for an open item once you're back in, or call the guest support line if you still can't sign in at all.

faq.question: How long does account restoration usually take?
faq.answer: PayPal says it tries to review submitted documents within two business days, though it states plainly that some cases take longer.

faq.question: Why did my account get limited in the first place?
faq.answer: PayPal's documentation groups the causes into four types: regulatory requirements (like requesting a debit card), Acceptable Use Policy violations, fraud protection after an unauthorized login or bank alert, and high-risk seller activity such as a spike in chargebacks or sales volume.

faq.question: Can I contact support if I can't log in at all?
faq.answer: Yes. Go to Contact Us, select Call Us, then "Call us as a guest" for the phone number. Have your account's phone number, a statement for the linked bank or card, and your registration email ready to confirm ownership.

faq.question: Will I lose my transaction history if my account is limited?
faq.answer: No. History stays intact and becomes fully accessible again once the restriction lifts.

faq.question: What's the fastest way to clear a lock caused by failed logins?
faq.answer: Reset your password from the Security tab in account settings. If the restriction doesn't clear afterward, it's likely tied to something other than the failed logins, and the Resolution Center is the next place to check.

faq.question: My identity verification photo keeps getting rejected. Now what?
faq.answer: Switch to the PayPal app's biometric option, which scans your ID and face directly through the camera, instead of uploading a photo. If you stick with uploading, make sure the whole document is visible and well-lit, and that any proof of address is dated within the last 12 months.
